title: Supreme Court Restores Trump Mass Voter Verification System
detail: The US Supreme Court restored the Trump administration's mass voter verification system, lifting lower-court restrictions on the controversial citizen voter database. The ruling allows the administration to proceed with large-scale voter roll verification efforts that critics have argued could suppress legitimate voter registrations.

media.caption: Supreme Court lifts restrictions on Trump voter verification database

title: Trump Administration Uses 'Pocket Rescission' to Cancel $810M in Approved Spending
detail: The White House canceled roughly $810 million in congressionally approved spending — including $567 million from HHS refugee and unaccompanied-minor services, plus migrant education, DOJ racial-tension programs, minority business development and housing counseling funds — using a 'pocket rescission' that runs out the 45-day congressional review clock before the fiscal year ends. The GAO has found the tactic unlawful under the Impoundment Control Act; Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins called it illegal, and Sen. Patty Murray accused the administration of ignoring Congress's spending laws.

media.caption: Trump administration cancels $810 million in approved HHS and related spending via pocket rescission
